request.spec:
My clients add up the lines on my invoices and get a different total from mine. Round each
line's quantity times unit price to the cent first (half up), and make the invoice total the
sum of those rounded line amounts.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for this implementation's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
My clients add up the lines on my invoices and get a different total from mine. Round each
line's quantity times unit price to the cent first (half up), and make the invoice total the
sum of those rounded line amounts.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Invoice totals now match what your clients get when they add up the lines. Each line's quantity × unit price is rounded half up to the cent first, and the invoice total is the sum of those rounded amounts. `bin/e2e` passes, including the check that earlier test data still seeds and reads back correctly.

**What changed:**
- **`InvoiceLine.amount()`** now rounds each line half up to the cent. Before, it returned the exact, unrounded product.
- **`Invoice.total()`** now just adds up those rounded line amounts. Before, it added the exact products and rounded only once at the end, which is why totals could differ by a cent.
- **Front end:** no logic change. It already displays the total the server sends. I only updated the comment in `invoice.service.ts` that described the old rule.

**Example from the test invoice:** the three lines come to 25.625, 22.575 and 0.525. These now round to 25.63, 22.58 and 0.53, giving a total of **$48.74**. The old rule gave **$48.73**.

No stored data or schema changes were needed. This also means totals on existing invoices may go up or down by a cent or so when shown under the new rule.
